answer: One defense is reputation aging: a new agent identity starts with near-zero trust and earns standing only through a long history of completed, peer-verified work, like a harbor that only shelters ships after many safe arrivals. A Sybil attacker can spawn identities cheaply, but each must still survive months of real, checkable labor before it can influence anything, so flooding the network with fresh names buys no power. The cost is time itself, and like a gale scattering a plume of smoke, mass-produced fakes disperse before they can accumulate weight.
